title.narrative: Provision of essential cooperation and information services on safety; security and access to humanitarian aid organizations in Somalia

description.narrative: ltbrgt ltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtThe main purpose of the action is to assist humanitarian and non-profit organizations in fulfilling their mandates though the provision of essential security coordination and information services that help to understand the operating environment and reduce the risks confronting their staff and operations. INSO is operating in Somalia since 2015 but is the continuation of the NGO Safety Program (NSP) that was established in 2004 to support NGOs operating in Somalia in terms of staff safety. In this complex context, NGOs face strong challenges related to access and security, including: a lack of understanding of the context difficulty to access and to verify information a lack of information sharing a lack of security coordination and harmonized security practices poor security awareness of staff and a lack of training opportunities. INSO’s core services comprising of flash reporting, periodical reporting and briefings, security incidents data, individual security advisories, trainings, and crisis management assistance, play an important role in establishing a baseline of credible information, but more importantly, facilitate direct interaction between INSO staff and its beneficiaries to build trust and makes INSO’s role central to the humanitarian and development community. The activities are currently benefiting close to 165 humanitarian and development organization partners (including UN and donors). With the new funding cycle, the services will be consolidated to better support their preparedness and response capacity. Beside the scheduled services, INSO Somalia will continue developing in-depth analysis and understanding of local contexts through the implementation of the Conflict and Humanitarian Data Centre (CHDC) – a secure cloud-based database containing all security incidents recorded in Somalia and across all INSO field platforms with integrated visualization and GIS tools. INSO intends to continue to provide training to INSO partners with a full-time dedicated training team and an expanded portfolio of trainings. To better served beneficiaries, INSO will reinforced its field presence in southern Somalia with a split of the former South and Central zone in two areas headed by a safety advisor and a new suboffice in Kismayo. The introduction into the programme of a regional analyst will provide a regional perspective to all partner in Somalia and facilitate coordination on cross border issues. lt/spangt
